Before we proceed, per our incident-response protocol, I'll need each responsible counsel from the participating functions to report their relevant findings. Let's start with whoever is ready to brief us on their area.

transcript.text: I need to report a critical finding from my review of the cloud-access logs. I've confirmed that exactly 2,736 accounts had both names and email addresses exposed together with unencrypted Social Security numbers. I want to flag that the preliminary incident summary still lists the record count as 'undetermined' because the forensic reconciliation was completed after that summary circulated. The notification package needs to reflect the confirmed count of 2,736 accounts before we proceed with approval.

transcript.text: I have a critical finding from my review. I checked the current state regulator incident portal and confirmed that, for this incident's data elements, the Massachusetts Attorney General filing must be submitted no later than the same day as the consumer notices. The filing sequence is absent from the draft package because the portal instruction changed this month. We need to update the package to reflect this same-day filing requirement before approval.

transcript.text: I have a critical finding from my review of the cyber policy. I confirmed that the endorsement requires written insurer consent before we promise identity-restoration services or any other remediation benefits to affected customers. I received the endorsement amendment from the broker yesterday, but I have not yet added this requirement to the notification checklist. We need to ensure the package reflects this written-consent requirement before approval, so we don't jeopardize coverage.
